B05_00: Commissural axons must cross the nervous system midline exactly once, and SLIT-ROBO signalling makes this possible. Before crossing, Netrin-1 acting on DCC attracts axons to the floor plate while ROBO3 suppresses ROBO1/2 repulsion to SLITs and NELL2 keeps them on course. After crossing, SLIT-bound ROBO silences DCC attraction and ROBO3 is downregulated, preventing re-crossing; ROBO3 loss causes horizontal gaze palsy with progressive scoliosis.
B05_01: Sema4D binding to plexin-B1 remodels actin, promoting endothelial migration in angiogenesis but collapsing neuronal growth cones. Plexin-B1 recruits the RhoA exchange factors ARHGEF11 and ARHGEF12, binds RND1, and with ERBB2 in endothelium activates RhoA, RhoB and RhoC. ROCK then phosphorylates myosin light chains and activates LIM kinases, generating myosin II contractility, stress fibres and stable adhesions, a Rho-dependent branch distinct from R-Ras plexin signalling.
B05_02: ROBO axon guidance receptors steer axons away from midline Slit, and the scaffold AKAP5 binds ROBO2 and the ROBO3.1 isoform to bring protein kinase A, protein kinase C and calcineurin close to the receptor. This lets guidance signalling integrate cAMP and calcium cues, and recruited PKC phosphorylates ROBO3.1. The complex has been shown in brain tissue, but its downstream consequences remain undefined.
B05_03: CHL1 is an immunoglobulin-superfamily adhesion receptor on neurons and glia that supports neuronal survival, neurite extension and axon steering. Lacking homophilic binding, it signals through partners: contactin-6, beta1 integrins via RGD and DGEA motifs, and neuropilin-1, through which it mediates Semaphorin-3A-induced growth cone repulsion. Ankyrin links it to the spectrin cytoskeleton, and CHL1 loss is associated with abnormal axon targeting and neurodevelopmental deficits.
B05_04: Growth cones advance by gripping the substrate at the front and releasing at the back, an asymmetry maintained by recycling the adhesion molecule L1CAM, which couples extracellular ligands to retrograde actin flow via ERM proteins. SRC phosphorylation of a tail tyrosine motif blocks AP-2 binding, while dephosphorylation allows clathrin- and dynamin-dependent endocytosis and kinesin-driven return to the leading edge. L1CAM mutations cause X-linked hydrocephalus and corpus callosum agenesis.
B05_05: Netrin-1 can repel as well as attract axons, and repulsion acts through UNC5A-D receptors, which also serve in vascular patterning and as dependence receptors that trigger death when unbound. Netrin binding promotes phosphorylation of the UNC5 ZU-5 domain, with Src-family kinases and SHP2 relaying signals to the growth cone actin cytoskeleton. Long-range repulsion requires DCC pairing with UNC5, and loss causes misrouted commissures.
B05_06: DSCAM and DSCAML1 are immunoglobulin-superfamily neuronal adhesion receptors whose homophilic binding mediates self-recognition and repulsion, setting neurite spacing, dendritic tiling and retinal mosaic arrangement. DSCAM also cooperates with the netrin receptor DCC to mediate netrin-1 attraction of commissural axons. The gene lies in the Down syndrome region of chromosome 21, though a causal role is unproven, and the interactions support axon pathfinding and circuit wiring precision.
B05_07: NrCAM is an L1-family adhesion receptor that aids axon guidance, assembly of nodes of Ranvier and eye development, with loss linked to guidance and lens defects. An ankyrin-binding segment couples it to the spectrin cytoskeleton, and a PDZ-binding motif engages SAP97, SAP102 and PSD-95 scaffolds. Extracellularly it binds the contactin axonin-1/TAG-1 to promote neurite outgrowth and partners neuropilin-2 in semaphorin-induced repulsion.
B05_08: Ankyrin-G, ankyrin-B and ankyrin-R tether the L1-family adhesion molecules L1CAM, neurofascin and NrCAM, together with sodium and KCNQ2/3 potassium channels, to spectrin-actin networks. This restrains diffusion and strengthens adhesion, supporting axon guidance, branching and inhibitory neuron synaptogenesis, and concentrates sodium channels at axon initial segments and nodes for reliable action potentials. Defects cause hydrocephalus, spastic paraplegia, epilepsy, arrhythmia and hereditary spherocytosis.
B05_09: Beyond the canonical class 3-plexin-A route, many transmembrane and GPI-anchored semaphorins engage plexins of the A, B, C and D subfamilies and non-plexin partners, steering axon repulsion, vascular patterning, bone remodelling and immune behaviour. Examples include SEMA4D with CD72 on B cells, SEMA7A with integrin alpha1/beta1, SEMA6D with TREM2-TYROBP in myeloid cells, and SEMA3E-PLXND1 limiting endothelial sprouting. Loss causes miswiring and abnormal vessels and immunity.
B05_10: In one branch of SLIT-ROBO signalling, SLIT2 binding to ROBO1 inhibits the RHOA GTPase-activating function of the myosin MYO9B, raising active RHOA. This activates ROCK and myosin light chain phosphorylation, producing the actomyosin contractility cranial motor axons need to follow SLIT cues, and limiting cell migration, with loss linked to lung cancer invasiveness. The receptor thus raises GTPase activity by inhibiting an inhibitor.
B05_11: Neurofascin is an L1-family adhesion molecule that organises nodes of Ranvier and axo-glial junctions needed for saltatory conduction. The neuronal 186 kDa isoform clusters at nodes with NrCAM and ankyrin, while the glial 155 kDa form partners contactin and CNTNAP1 to build paranodal junctions; a PDZ-binding motif recruits syntenin-1, and doublecortin reflects developmental roles. Disruption causes conduction failure, and neurofascin is an autoantigen in inflammatory neuropathy.
B05_12: Cortical pyramidal neurons elaborate dendritic arbors that set how many synapses they receive, and the axon-repelling cue SLIT1 is reused here to promote branching. SLIT1 binding to ROBO1 and ROBO2 on dendrites, with the adaptor NCK2 coupling ROBO to actin regulators, creates new branch points rather than retraction. Disturbed dendrite branching yields simplified arbors and altered connectivity associated with neurodevelopmental and intellectual disability phenotypes.
B05_13: Netrin-1 attracts commissural axons across the spinal cord midline, and whether growth cones turn toward or away depends on second messengers; DCC mutations cause congenital mirror movements and corpus callosum agenesis. Netrin binding to DCC activates phospholipase C gamma to produce IP3 and diacylglycerol, releasing ER calcium and gating TRPC3 and TRPC6 channels. The resulting calcium influx, tuned by cyclic nucleotides, determines attraction versus repulsion.
B05_14: Forward signalling from ephrin-B-bound EphB receptors shapes dendritic spines during brain development, turning motile filopodia into mature mushroom spines with recruited NMDA receptors. Clustered receptors engage Src-family kinases, FAK and exchange factors such as intersectin and kalirin, activating CDC42 and RAC1 for Arp2/3 actin branching and PAK signalling, while RHOA-ROCK-LIMK phosphorylates cofilin. Loss leaves spines immature and synapses sparse; the receptors also guide axons.
B05_15: Sema3A repels axons by binding neuropilin-1, which pairs with a plexin-A to collapse the growth cone, here by switching off substrate adhesion so the neurite loses traction and turns away. Plexin GAP activity toward R-Ras lowers integrin affinity, while Rnd1, Rac1, FARP2 and Src-family and Fes kinases relay signalling, and talin and PIP5K1C link to focal adhesions. Disruption misroutes peripheral and central axons.
B05_16: Semaphorin 4D acting through plexin-B1 causes loss of integrin adhesion and leading-edge collapse in axon guidance, and in vascular and tumour settings plexin-B1 partners MET. Rnd1 activates the plexin GAP domain, lowering R-Ras, PI3K and Akt so that GSK-3beta inactivates CRMP2. In parallel, p190RhoGAP transiently reduces RhoA-GTP and Rac1 is redirected, so actin and microtubule dynamics favour retraction.
B05_17: SLIT and ROBO levels determine how neurons respond to midline guidance cues, and this covers their regulation from gene to receptor. LIM-homeodomain factors and HOXA2 drive cell-type-specific transcription, and MSI1 boosts ROBO3 translation using ribosomal, cap-binding and decay machinery. Ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, opposed by USP33 for ROBO1, tune protein levels, while dystroglycan and collagen IV anchor SLITs; misregulation contributes to guidance defects and cancer invasion.
B05_18: Ephrin-B and EPH receptor contact signals bidirectionally, and reverse signalling into the ephrin-bearing cell steers growth cones, sets tissue boundaries and shapes spines; ephrin-B1 loss causes craniofrontonasal defects. FYN and SRC phosphorylate the ephrin tail, recruiting NCK2 and, via GIT1, ARHGEF7 and PAK, driving RAC1-dependent actin and myosin remodelling. Alternatively, a PDZ-binding motif engages scaffolds such as syntenin for junctional and synaptic organisation.
B05_19: RAC1 activation converts a repulsive cue into growth cone actin remodelling as axons decide whether to cross the midline, with basal RAC1 sustaining outgrowth; loss causes midline crossing errors. SLIT2 binding to ROBO1 exposes motifs that recruit NCK1 or NCK2, which bring SOS1 and SOS2 to load GTP onto RAC1. Active RAC1 engages PAK kinases, linking receptor occupancy to actin and adhesion dynamics.
B05_20: Sema3A is a classic axon repellent that collapses growth cones, keeping sensory and cortical projections out of inappropriate territory and patterning nerves and dendrites. Signalling requires neuropilin-1 and a plexin-A, and in the PAK-dependent arm Rac1 activates group I PAKs, which phosphorylate LIMK1 to inactivate cofilin and remodel actin. Src-family and Fes kinases and HSP90 support transmission, and loss leaves axons insensitive and mistargeted.
B05_21: EPH-ephrin contact usually leads to withdrawal, steering growth cones and cells away, patterning retinotopic maps, guiding commissural and corticospinal axons and sharpening boundaries. Because binding is high-affinity, ADAM10, matrix metalloproteinases and gamma-secretase cleave the complex, and clathrin-, AP-2- and dynamin-dependent endocytosis internalise it. Src-family kinases transmit the signal, while RAC1 activated by TIAM1 and VAV drives actin remodelling and growth cone collapse.
B05_22: L1CAM acts as a receptor converting extracellular contact into axon growth, guidance and migration decisions, and its mutations cause X-linked hydrocephalus with corticospinal and corpus callosum defects. Partnering beta1 and beta3 integrins, L1 triggers Src, VAV2, RAC1, PAK1 and MEK-ERK signalling for outgrowth. It is also an obligate co-receptor with neuropilin-1 for Sema3A collapse, mediates homophilic attraction, and is modulated by FGFR1 and casein kinase 2.
B05_23: Collapsin response mediator proteins convert the repellent Sema3A, acting through neuropilin-1 and plexin-A, into growth cone collapse. The plexin tail holds CRMP1 and DPYSL proteins near kinases, and sequential phosphorylation by Fyn-recruited Cdk5/p35, Fes and GSK3beta stops CRMPs binding tubulin, stalling microtubule assembly and depolymerising F-actin. This patterns cortical and sensory projections, and CRMP phosphorylation recurs in neurodegeneration and failed nerve regeneration.
B05_24: Ephrin-A binding to EPHA receptors makes growth cones collapse and retract, keeping axons out of ephrin-rich territory and ordering topographic maps such as the retinocollicular projection. Clustered receptors recruit Src-family kinases that switch ephexin toward RHOA activation while Cdc42 and Rac1 signalling falls. RHOA then drives ROCK-mediated myosin light chain phosphorylation and myosin II contraction, disassembling filopodia and lamellipodia into directed retraction.
B05_25: DCC converts netrin-1 gradients into attraction, guiding commissural axons across the midline; loss causes congenital mirror movements and corpus callosum agenesis. Lacking catalytic activity, DCC associates with FAK, Src and Fyn, which phosphorylate it on netrin binding and recruit NCK1 and DOCK1. These activate RAC1, CDC42 and TRIO, with WASL and ABLIM proteins remodelling actin to drive asymmetric filopodial extension toward netrin.
B05_26: In this SLIT-ROBO branch, inactivation of CDC42 and RAC1 collapses growth cone protrusions, governing repulsive guidance, midline crossing and cortical neuron positioning; SRGAP gene disruption is linked to intellectual disability and migration defects. SLIT2 binding to ROBO1 recruits the GAPs SRGAP1-3 and ARHGAP39, which stimulate GTP hydrolysis on CDC42 and RAC1. Lower Rho GTPase activity withdraws filopodial and lamellipodial drive.
B05_27: ABL kinases convert SLIT-ROBO repulsion into cytoskeletal change, determining whether commissural axons cross the midline once, and the axis also acts in epithelial polarity and tumour migration. ABL1 and ABL2 phosphorylate growth cone effectors and ROBO1 itself, tuning receptor sensitivity. Their partners CAP1 and CAP2 govern actin turnover while CLASP1 and CLASP2 act on microtubule plus ends, coordinating filopodial collapse with microtubule behaviour.
